B5: Vertical stratification from the LiDAR point cloud

Source: R/indicateur_b5_stratification.R
indicateur_b5_stratification.Rd

Vertical structure of each unit read in the LiDAR point cloud itself, not in a canopy height model: Shannon entropy of the distribution of returns (or of foliage density) between five height strata, on 0-100 (100 = even distribution between the strata). B2 reads the canopy surface seen from above; B5 reads what lies under it (spec 067, chantier C, first step, without ForPT). Source-conditional: without a point cloud, B5 is NA with its status and the B family is unchanged.

Usage

indicateur_b5_stratification(
  units,
  nuage = NULL,
  layers = NULL,
  strates = c(0, 2, 5, 10, 20),
  profil = c("points", "densite_foliaire"),
  normaliser = FALSE,
  hauteur_sol = 0.5,
  hauteur_max = 60,
  classes = c(1:5, 9),
  min_points = 100L,
  resolution = 1
)

Arguments

units

sf polygon layer (spatial units / UGF).

nuage

The point cloud, one of:

  • a data.frame (or matrix) with columns X, Y, Z, and optionally Classification, in the CRS of units;

  • a LAS object of lidR;

  • a character vector of .laz / .las files, or a directory holding them (e.g. <project>/cache/layers/lidar_nuage), read tile by tile with lidR (in Suggests) and clipped to the units.

NULL: B5 is NA with status skipped_no_lidar.

layers

Unused, accepted for nemeton_compute().

strates

Numeric. Lower bounds of the strata in metres, starting at 0. Default c(0, 2, 5, 10, 20): strata 0-2, 2-5, 5-10, 10-20 and20 m (spec 067).

profil

"points" (default, spec 067 D-3): share of vegetation returns in each stratum. "densite_foliaire": share of foliage density in each stratum, from the gap fraction (MacArthur & Horn 1969), which corrects part of the occlusion of the lower strata by the upper ones.

normaliser

Logical. Are Z values altitudes that must first be turned into heights above ground? TRUE needs lidR and ground returns (class 2): heights are taken above a TIN of the ground returns, tile by tile. Default FALSE (heights already normalised). A cloud whose median Z exceeds hauteur_max is refused rather than read as heights.

hauteur_sol

Numeric. Returns below this height (m) are ground: they count in no stratum, but they enter the gap fraction of "densite_foliaire". Default 0.5.

hauteur_max

Numeric. Returns above this height (m) are noise and dropped, as are returns below -1 m. Default 60.

classes

Integer. Classification codes kept when the cloud has a Classification column. Default c(1:5, 9): unclassified, ground, the three vegetation classes and water of IGN LiDAR HD; buildings (6), noise (7, 18), bridges (17) and the IGN classes 64-67 are dropped.

min_points

Integer. Minimum number of returns in a unit (ground included); below it, B5 is NA with status skipped_low_density. Default 100.

resolution

Numeric. Size (m) of the grid used to assign returns to units (a return belongs to the unit holding the centre of its cell). Default 1.

Value

units with

B5

score 0-100, 100 = returns (or foliage) evenly spread over the strata; 0 = a single stratum, or no vegetation above hauteur_sol.

b5_status

calculated, skipped_no_lidar, skipped_no_coverage (no return in the unit) or skipped_low_density (fewer than min_points).

b5_profil

profil used.

b5_points

number of returns in the unit (ground included).

b5_densite

returns per square metre.

b5_s1, ..., b5_sK

share of each stratum (sums to 1), from the lowest to the highest.

Details

Score. With p_k the share of stratum k among K strata, B5 = 100 * (-sum(p_k * log(p_k)) / log(K)): the Shannon entropy normalised by its maximum, i.e. the evenness of the vertical profile. It is the LiDAR form of the foliage height diversity of MacArthur & MacArthur (1961). It needs no ForPT (spec 067, D-3); ForPT will be used later to separate wood from foliage.

"densite_foliaire". With P(h) the share of returns below height h (ground included), the foliage of stratum [a, b) is proportional to log(P(b) / P(a)) (MacArthur & Horn 1969; the extinction coefficient cancels out in the shares). A unit without ground return gets a floor of half a return at hauteur_sol.

Pitfalls (fiche B5): at about 10 returns per square metre (LiDAR HD), the lower strata of closed stands are under-sampled, so "points" underestimates the stratification of closed stands (measured by the dimensioning of spec 067); a leaf-on and a leaf-off flight do not give the same profile; B5 measures evenness, not height: a 2 m thicket split between two strata can score as high as a high forest.

Lifecycle

Experimental (spec 067): may change in any release.

References

MacArthur, R. H. & MacArthur, J. W. (1961). On bird species diversity. Ecology 42(3), 594-598.

MacArthur, R. H. & Horn, H. S. (1969). Foliage profile by vertical measurements. Ecology 50(5), 802-804.

See also

indicateur_b2_structure(), compute_dtm_chm_from_laz()

Examples

units <- sf::st_sf(
  id = 1:2,
  geometry = sf::st_sfc(
    sf::st_polygon(list(rbind(c(0, 0), c(20, 0), c(20, 20), c(0, 20), c(0, 0)))),
    sf::st_polygon(list(rbind(c(20, 0), c(40, 0), c(40, 20), c(20, 20), c(20, 0)))),
    crs = 2154
  )
)
set.seed(1)
n <- 4000
nuage <- data.frame(X = runif(n, 0, 40), Y = runif(n, 0, 20))
# unit 1: one high layer; unit 2: returns spread over the whole height
nuage$Z <- ifelse(nuage$X < 20, runif(n, 22, 28), runif(n, 0, 30))
indicateur_b5_stratification(units, nuage)$B5
#> [1]  0.00 88.76
